note: The Solana toolchain as DATA. A toolchain bump is an edit to this file and
nothing else: no Kotlin changes, no release. Every component is fetched from
its own upstream (docs/SOLANA.md, 'Where the toolchain comes from') — we host
nothing and mirror nothing.
Order is INSTALL order, and it is also the order the Setup screen lists.
Two orderings in it are load-bearing:
* platform-tools is linked into rustup by its own postInstall, so rustup
must already be there when it lands;
* apt comes after the three small binaries so the editor, the language
server and the agent are usable before the slow package step, and before
the two crates that need a C compiler to build.
sha256 is over the downloaded file exactly as served. It is also the
component's revision: change the hash and that one row re-installs, while
every other row stays where it is.

components.name: Debian userland
components.summary: A real Debian under proot. apt works; we maintain none of it.
note: No url and no sha256 here on purpose: this one is the existing
UserlandInstaller/DebianUserland path, which resolves Debian's own
container image through the registry and verifies the registry's digest
as it streams. Duplicating a pinned hash here would pin a tag that moves.
It is also the one archive unpacked THROUGH proot rather than beside it,
because Debian's image carries a hard link (perl) that a host tar cannot
reproduce into app storage — see docs/SOLANA.md, 'Living with proot'.

components.name: rustup (manager only)
components.summary: The toolchain manager with no toolchain. cargo-build-sbf execs it.
note: --default-toolchain none downloads no rustc at all: platform-tools already
carries one, and a second Rust would be 1.5 GB we do not need. rustup is
here because cargo-build-sbf shells out to it and dies with 'Failed to
execute rustup' otherwise (docs/SOLANA.md).
static.rust-lang.org publishes a .sha256 beside every archived rustup-init;
the hash below is that file's, for 1.29.0/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.

components.name: SBF platform-tools
components.summary: The SBF compiler: its own cargo, rustc and an LLVM with the SBF backend.
note: The load-bearing component. 505 MB down, ~1.4 GB unpacked, and the only
reason a Solana program can be compiled on this device at all.
Unpacked with the host's tar straight into the rootfs — pushing 1.4 GB of
small files through proot's ptrace is many times slower, and this archive
has no hard link to trip over.
postInstall is where rustup is pointed at it. Without the link and the
default, rustup's cargo shim resolves to nothing and every build fails
with a message about a missing toolchain.

components.name: rust-analyzer
components.summary: The language server: completion, go-to-definition, the squiggles.
components.note: A gzipped ELF, not a tarball. Ungzipped on this side and chmod 755'd.

components.name: Spettro (agent)
components.summary: The bundled ACP agent. One static binary, no Node anywhere.
note: Unpacked into the same /opt/seeker/agents/<id> layout the agent picker
uses (solana/agents/AgentCatalog.kt, GUEST_INSTALL_ROOT), so an agent
installed by Setup and one installed from the picker are the same thing
in the same place. ACP is behind -acp / --acp; the picker probes it.

components.name: Build tools (apt)
components.summary: gcc, git, pkg-config, OpenSSL headers — what building a crate needs.
note: The one step that runs under proot's --link2symlink, because dpkg unpacks
hard links and cannot work without it. Nothing else may use that flag:
under it cargo install hard-links its finished binary out of a scratch
directory it then deletes, reports success, and leaves a dangling symlink
(docs/SOLANA.md, 'Living with proot').
Sizes are apt's, not ours, so they are estimates and the row says so.

components.name: cargo-build-sbf
components.summary: The build driver. No arm64 binary exists upstream, so the phone builds it.
note: Measured on the device: 3 min 45 s wall, 21 min CPU. There is no arm64
Linux binary of this anywhere, and this is the one step that removes the
need for us to host one.
Runs through proot WITHOUT --link2symlink. Under that flag it finishes,
says 'Installed package', and leaves a symlink to a scratch directory that
no longer exists — which is why 'marker' is checked as a real file on this
side afterwards and 'verify' is then run in the guest.

components.name: Anchor
components.summary: The Anchor CLI. Also built here: it ships no release binaries at all.
note: --locked, because anchor-cli's own Cargo.lock is the only combination its
releases are tested against. Same proot rule as cargo-build-sbf.
Not required: a Native program builds without it, and Setup must not make
the whole toolchain hostage to the longest compile in it.
